page.layout: One column of running text, centred on the page, with the page number above it. No marginal notes. At the right edge a sliver of the facing page is visible; it is cut off and is not transcribed. The catchword sits at the lower right.

main_text.p: conjurationes plus quam Catilina-rias exercere, infames quoscunq; & scelleratos[?] ad societatem suâ ad-mittere ; Ordinariis obedientiam subtrahere, multas in utraq; politia rebelliones & schismata inducere, magis ad ecclesiæ destructionem quàm ædificationem facere, ideoq; tam à curiâ, quam à Sorbonâ esse e-jectos. Vide Benedicti Ariæ Montani (qui fuit non solùm Romanus catholicus, sed etiam Hispanus) ju-dicium & vaticinium de Jesuitis, q; exstat in Bibliis interlinearibus, editis Antwerpiæ ann. 1584. Item Arestum supremæ curiæ Parisiensis incisum aureis literis pyramidi ex ni-gro marmore exstructæ Lutetiæ, quam multa millia testium omni exceptione majorum suis oculis viderunt, palparunt, legerunt, licet tandem ad Jesuitarum preces sit lo-co remota. Plura etiam petito ex oratione ad regem Christianissimū perscriptâ, de restitutione Jesui-tarum in regno Galliæ.

page.notes: Printed text is set in the old long-s form, transcribed here as plain s. "scelleratos" is read from a worn word and marked [?]. The word "Galliæ" closes the paragraph on a short line; the printed line reads "Gallix" with a ligature, read as Galliæ. The sliver of the facing page at the right edge is excluded as the neighbouring page.
